page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine configured with 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 2835 GB NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark evaluations, the E48ds_v7 demonstrates strong performance in data compression and cryptography, scoring in the top 25% for single-threaded gzip compression, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU encryption tests. Memory performance is balanced, with uncached large-block read bandwidth at 162.68 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 66.17 GB/sec. Database and key-value operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by strong Redis SET performance reaching 76.28 million operations per second.

While the server excels at prompt processing for small and medium language models, text generation for large 70B models is a relative bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% of benchmarks. This highlights a tradeoff where CPU-based inference is highly capable for smaller models but limited for massive parameter scales. Given its high memory density, fast local NVMe storage, and strong cryptographic and compression capabilities, the E48ds_v7 is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads. It is highly suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data warehousing, and enterprise-grade web serving.
